Q25409451.summary: Bishop Marianos of Faras stands in rich vestments, a book in his hand, beside the Virgin, who holds the Christ Child on her left arm. A full-length figure of the adult Christ originally stood at the bishop's side and laid his hand on Marianos's shoulder, but only fragments of it survive. Painted when Marianos took office, the image placed the Nubian bishop under the protection of Christ and his Mother.
facts: Marianos was bishop of Faras from 1005 to 1036; the painting is one of fourteen bishop portraits found in Faras Cathedral.
It was discovered by Polish archaeologists during the UNESCO-sponsored Nubian campaign of the 1960s and has been in the National Museum in Warsaw since 1964.
Of the adult Christ, only the nimbus, part of the leg and garment, and the fingers resting on the bishop's shoulder remain.

links.label: Wikipedia (pl): Biskup Marianos pod opieką Chrystusa i Matki Boskiej

Q25409451.notes: Wikidata labels the style 'Coptic art'; it is Nubian (Makurian) painting. The Christ Child is clearly visible; the adult Christ survives only in fragments.

commons:8915912.summary: Against a gold ground, the Virgin holds the infant Christ while Joseph stands close beside her, and a priest stretches out his hands to them before a domed sanctuary at the right; a mountain with trees rises at the left. The miniature marks the feast of Christ's Circumcision on the first of January, when the Child received the name Jesus. Its graceful figures and modelled landscape show the classicising refinement of Constantinople's court painters around the year 1000.
facts: The Menologion of Basil II, made in Constantinople for Emperor Basil II (r. 976–1025), contains some 430 miniatures and covers only the half of the church year from September to February.
Unusually, the names of eight painters, including Pantoleon, are written beside the miniatures, though all in the same scribe's hand.
The manuscript was owned in the 15th century by Ludovico Sforza, Duke of Milan, and given to Pope Paul V in the early 17th century; it is now Vat. gr. 1613.
commons:8915912.notes: The Commons description places this miniature on f. 287 and gives an 11th-century date; Wikipedia dates the manuscript c. 1000 (between 979 and the early 11th century). The painter's name for this miniature was not checked.

cur:catacombs-cordoba-sarcophagus.summary: Columns divide the front into niches with Old and New Testament scenes – among them the Fall of Adam and Eve and Moses striking the rock – and the deceased, alongside scenes of Christ. Found in Córdoba itself, it is one of the finest early Christian sarcophagi in Spain.
facts: The museum dates it to the first third of the 4th century and records that it was found in the city of Córdoba.
Commons has detailed photographs of its Original Sin and Moses scenes.
cur:catacombs-cordoba-sarcophagus.notes: The Christ scenes were not individually verified.

cur:objects-lorsch-gospels-front-cover-v.summary: Five ivory panels form one of the grandest Carolingian book covers: at the top two angels hold a medallion with the bust of Christ blessing; in the centre the Virgin sits enthroned with the Christ Child, between St John the Baptist and the prophet Zacharias; and at the bottom are the Nativity and the Annunciation to the Shepherds. Classical architecture and drapery show how deliberately Charlemagne's artists revived the art of Late Antiquity. The cover proclaims the Incarnation: the eternal Son, blessing from heaven, born of the Virgin.
facts: The V&A explains that the panels formed the front cover of the Lorsch Gospels, a Gospel book of about 810 listed in the Lorsch abbey library catalogue of about 860; the back cover, with Christ treading on the beasts, is in the Museo Sacro of the Vatican.
The manuscript was taken to Heidelberg in 1556 with the Bibliotheca Palatina and divided; its first volume is now in Alba Iulia (Batthyaneum) and the second in the Vatican.
In 2023 UNESCO inscribed the whole group of ivories and manuscripts in its Memory of the World register.
cur:objects-lorsch-gospels-front-cover-v.notes: Companion of the existing featured entry 'lorsch-gospels-ivory-christ-treading-beasts' (Vatican back cover); this is a separate object.
